[[File:Βαρώτσος Κωνσταντίνος.jpg|thumb]]
'''Costas Varotsos''' ({{langx|el|Κώστας Βαρώτσος}}; born 14 August 1956) is a Greek [[physicist]] known from his contribution to the global climate-dynamics research and [[remote sensing]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite web|author= |url=http://orcid.org/0000-0001-7215-3610 |title=Prof. Dr. Costas Varotsos CV |date= |access-date=2013-10-07}}</ref>

==Work==
Varotsos pointed out the occurrence of major [[sudden stratospheric warming]] over [[Antarctica]] in September 2002, an event which resulted in both the smaller-sized [[ozone hole]] over [[Antarctica]] and its splitting into two holes.<ref name="auto1">{{cite journal|author= Kondratyev, K. Ya |author2=A. P. Cracknell |title= Preface |date= 2005-08-20|doi=10.1080/01431160500076087 |volume=26 |issue=16 |journal=International Journal of Remote Sensing |pages=3331–3332|bibcode=2005IJRS...26.3331. |s2cid=216151256 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Von Savigny, C.|display-authors=et al |title= The ozone hole breakup in September 2002 as seen by SCIAMACHY on ENVISAT |journal= Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences |volume= 62 |issue= 3 |pages= 721–734 |doi=10.1175/JAS-3328.1 |year= 2005 |bibcode=2005JAtS...62..721V |doi-access= free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Glatthor, Prior to September 2002, it was thought, that a major [[sudden stratospheric warming]] could happen only in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]. His follow-up work on this subject published in [[Eos]] Transactions - the official Journal of the [[American Geophysical Union]];<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Varotsos, C. |title=Why did a "no-ozone-hole" episode occur in Antarctica? |doi=10.1029/2003EO190007 |bibcode=2003EOSTr..84..183V |volume=84 |issue=19 |journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union |page=183|year=2003 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Jadin, E. A.|display-authors=et al |title= Influence of atmospheric circulation variations on the ozone layer |date= 2005-08-20|doi=10.1080/01431160500076541 |volume=26 |issue= 16 |journal=International Journal of Remote Sensing |pages=3467–3478|bibcode=2005IJRS...26.3467J |s2cid=128554498 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Semane, N.|display-authors=et al |title= An unusual stratospheric ozone decrease linked to isentropic air-mass transport as observed over Irene (25.5° S, 28.1° E) in mid-May 2002 |journal= Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics |volume= 6 |issue= 7 |pages= 1927–1936 |doi= 10.5194/acp-6-1927-2006 |year= 2006 |doi-access= free }}</ref> and the Europhysics News.

Varotsos suggested the [[fractal]] structure of the total [[ozone]] and [[temperature]] in the [[Earth's atmosphere]]. In 2005-2006 he showed that processes based on the nonlinear nature of the atmospheric dynamics could probably address the question “What caused the southern hemisphere to exhibit very strong planetary waves in 2002?” This evidence is based on his new finding that the fluctuations of the total ozone content and temperature exhibit long-range correlations.<ref>{{cite journal|author= Chattopadhyay, Goutami, and Surajit Chattopadhyay |title= Autoregressive forecast of monthly total ozone concentration: A neurocomputing approach  |date= September 2009|doi=10.1016/j.cageo.2008.11.007 |volume=35 |issue= 9 |journal=Computers & Geosciences |pages=1925–1932|bibcode= 2009CG.....35.1925C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Nerushev, A. F. (2008) |url= http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1451105 |title= Perturbations of the ozone layer induced by intense atmospheric vortices |journal= International Journal of Remote Sensing |volume= 29 |issue= 9 |pages= 2705–2732 |access-date=2013-12-02|doi= 10.1080/01431160701767526 |year= 2008 | bibcode=2008IJRS...29.2705N |s2cid = 129813186|url-access= subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author= Hu, Y., and Q. Series A, Mathematical, Physical, and Engineering Sciences |year= 2007 |volume= 365 |issue= 1861 |pages= 3061–84 |publisher= Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences, 365(1861), 3061-3084 |doi= 10.1098/rsta.2007.0020 |pmid= 17872361 |bibcode= 2007RSPTA.365.3061L |s2cid= 9054205 |access-date=2013-12-02|url-access= subscription }}</ref>

Varotsos has contributed to the fields of [[remote sensing]], [[atmospheric physics]] & [[chemistry]], and [[environmental change]] with 18 international books (monographs<ref name="auto2"/>) published by [[Springer Publishing]] during 2000–2025.
